items.item: `YAML.Limits.events` is never read, so the event-count limit is not enforced.
`.json` and `.core` resolve identically, because `resolve` shares one branch.
Schema resolution accepts any letter case for null, true and false, so `tRUE` becomes a b

notes: Event limit: the parser's private append now throws YAML.Parse.Error.eventLimit (existing case) when output.count reaches limits.events; the count includes stream/document start and end events. Resolution (YAML 1.2.2 ch.10): .json resolves only null, true, false, -?(0|[1-9][0-9]*) as integer and that plus optional fraction/exponent as floating; .core resolves null/Null/NULL/~, true/True/TRUE/false/False/FALSE, [-+]?[0-9]+, 0o octal, 0x hex (content normalized to decimal, as decimal integers already were), [-+]?(.d+|d+(.d*)?)([eE][-+]?d+)? and .inf/.nan spellings as floating. Decision: under .json a plain scalar matching no JSON form resolves to string rather than being an error as the spec says, because reporting it would need a new case on the @frozen public YAML.Compose.Error (API change); say if you want that. Behaviour change for users of the default .core: 'tRUE', 'nULL' etc. are now strings; '.inf', '0x1f', '0o17' now resolve to floating/integer instead of string. Only in-package uses found (swift-institute/institute has its own resolver).
